_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for BMY retrospectives (retro/build_bmy.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2003); the earnings 8-Ks of 2007-2009 were accepted before the open or during the session on their release days. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K; it also restates the year before when a business became a discontinued operation), the guides for the current fiscal year (each field from the latest guide that states it) and the latest declared dividend. Bristol-Myers Squibb's fiscal year is the calendar year. EPS is GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations: the company's non-GAAP EPS excludes upfront and milestone licensing payments, which recur, so it is shown and never used. 2001 is excluded and the history starts with 2002. Guides: GAAP EPS ranges (the current-FY EPS) and non-GAAP ranges (shown only); revenue growth is guided in words only, so BASE takes the latest quarter's net sales growth excluding foreign exchange as each release states it. A print's growth and margins are derived from the raw figures of its release ('raw', $ millions; the builder re-derives and checks them), each against the year-ago quarter as the same release shows it; U.S. and international net sales come from the release's supplemental exhibit. Rule T's raw figures are in 'rule_t'. No later fact enters through this file: every source's published date bounds its use.

history_vintages.why: 'The Company, through its divisions and subsidiaries, is engaged in the discovery, development, licensing, manufacturing, marketing, distribution and sale of pharmaceuticals and other health care related products.' (FY2006 10-K, Item 1); 'In the pharmaceutical industry, the majority of an innovative product’s commercial value is usually realized during the period in which the product has market exclusivity.' (Item 1); 'The Company faces competition from other pharmaceutical manufacturers, including from lower-priced generic products.' (Item 1A heading); 'The composition of matter patent for PLAVIX*, which expires in 2011, is currently the subject of patent litigation in the U.S. with Apotex Inc. and Apotex Corp. (Apotex)' (Item 1A)
history_vintages.normalization: diluted EPS from continuing operations, each year from the latest filing that reports it; GAAP throughout: the company's non-GAAP EPS excludes 'upfront and milestone payments for in-licensing of products that have not achieved regulatory approval' among its specified items, a cost listed in every year from 2005 to 2007 ($44M, $70M, $162M), so it does not exclude only one-offs (the NKE FY2007 and PFE rule) and is shown in the guide line only; 2002-2006 from the FY2006 10-K (Medical Imaging, ConvaTec and Mead Johnson in, OTN out); 2001 is excluded: $0.95 a diluted share from continuing operations (FY2005 10-K; $1,866M), while the items the FY2003 10-K/A lists as affecting the comparability of 2001 (acquired in-process research and development of $2,772 million for DuPont Pharmaceuticals, $588 million of restructuring and other items and $77 million of litigation charges, less $475 million of gains on sales of businesses) come to $1,905M after taxes, more than the year's earnings from continuing operations, so reported EPS is 49.5% of the EPS without them (under half), and no per-share figure excluding only one-offs was published; the history and the P/E window start with 2002 (the ACN FY02, AAPL FY2002 and PFE 2003 rule)

rule_t._doc: Rule T over fiscal 1997-2006, the decade of the FY2006 10-K (the vintage public on 2008-01-04): each year-on-year change from the latest 10-K (or 10-K/A) published by then that reports both years. U.S. and international net sales from the geographic data (international = the consolidated total less the United States; the FY1998 and FY1999 10-Ks state the United States before inter-area eliminations), the gross margin from the statements of earnings (net sales less cost of products sold), net sales growth and the pre-tax margin (earnings from continuing operations before minority interest and income taxes) from the five-year financial summaries. Seams stay in, as published: Clairol and Zimmer discontinued from the FY2000 10-K, the 2003 restatement (wholesaler inventory) in the FY2001 10-K/A and FY2002 10-K, the 2004 restatement in the FY2003 10-K/A, OTN discontinued from the FY2004 10-K, and 2001's acquired in-process research and development ($2,772 million, DuPont Pharmaceuticals) in its pre-tax earnings. Thresholds: XBULL the best year, BULL the median, BASE the worst, BEAR one median-to-worst step beyond the worst; whole percent and 10 bp, rounded half up.

price_basis: Yahoo's BMY series is adjusted for the 2-for-1 splits of 1997-03-03 and 1999-03-01 and books the 2001 Zimmer spin-off as a 1000000:951777 split on 2001-08-07; none follows 2001, so from 2002 Yahoo's close is the price as traded ($26.52 on 2007-12-31, the fourth-quarter 2007 low the FY2007 10-K reports). No per-share fact in this file was published before the 1999 split (every history year comes from a filing of 2003 or later), so 'splits' is empty; the spin-off factor is a 'distributions' record.
